topic: Most Rugby World Cup titles: South Africa 4 (1995, 2007, 2019, 2023); New Zealand 3 (1987, 2011, 2015); Australia 2 (1991, 1999); England 1 (2003). 1995 final at Ellis Park, Johannesburg; 2023 final at Stade de France, Saint-Denis, Paris: South Africa 12–11 New Zealand.
policy_note: Every spoken or shown fact → a claim with ≥ 2 independent publishers; core claims need a primary/scholarly source.

myths.myth: New Zealand has won the most Rugby World Cups because the All Blacks are the dominant team.
myths.reality: South Africa has four titles to New Zealand's three after beating the All Blacks 12–11 in the 2023 final.

britannica_rwc.title: Rugby World Cup
britannica_rwc.notes: South Africa four titles, New Zealand three, Australia two, England one; 1995 tournament hosted and won by South Africa a year after the end of apartheid

mandela_found.title: 1995 Rugby World Cup — Mandela and the Springbok jersey
mandela_found.notes: Mandela presented the trophy to captain Francois Pienaar at Ellis Park, Johannesburg, on 24 June 1995 wearing a Springbok jersey; the 1994 election had ended apartheid

britannica_mandela.title: Nelson Mandela
britannica_mandela.notes: elected president in April 1994 after the end of apartheid; 1995 Rugby World Cup a symbol of reconciliation
